record.what_it_does: AI meeting assistant that records, transcribes and summarizes meetings.
record.auth_notes: The Public API uses a static Bearer key that a user generates in workspace Developer settings (max 2 per user). It has no OAuth. The official hosted MCP server uses OAuth 2.1 with browser consent. There is no public OAuth app or client-registration path for the REST API, so a multi-user toolkit would have to use the MCP OAuth flow. That flow is reachable only through MCP clients. Everything here comes from a secondary source (Scalekit).
record.access_notes: Per Scalekit, the REST Public API is "available to Enterprise workspaces only", so it needs an Enterprise plan and a sales conversation. The hosted MCP server works from a standard Otter account via OAuth. I could not open Otter's own docs to confirm either claim.
record.api_breadth_notes: Base URL api.otter.ai/v1. Covers channels and members, conversations (list, retrieve, ingest a file via POST), audio download links, and workspace details. Rate limit is 10 requests per second. The MCP server exposes only three read-only tools: search meetings, fetch a transcript, and get the current user.
record.mcp_notes: https://mcp.otter.ai/mcp (Streamable HTTP, OAuth, read-only tools). Described as provider-hosted by Otter. Source is the Scalekit blog and the mcpservers.org listing. The help.otter.ai page returned 403.
record.blocker_notes: The REST API is limited to Enterprise workspaces and uses per-user static keys, which are awkward for multi-user OAuth-style distribution. The MCP server is open to standard accounts but exposes only 3 read-only tools. Whether Composio can register as an MCP OAuth client is unconfirmed.

evidence.quote: Otter runs a provider-hosted MCP server at mcp.otter.ai/mcp.
There is no public API key for the MCP server.
Otter webhooks push conversation and action-item events in real time.

record.needs_human: All facts come from a third-party blog (Scalekit). help.otter.ai returned 403 and otter.ai/api/docs rendered no content. Check Otter's official API docs for the Enterprise requirement, OpenAPI spec, webhook setup and any sandbox. Also check whether third-party MCP OAuth client registration is allowed.
